advice: Experiment: Keep the four ZA accumulators and existing tile mapping. Within each reduction step, issue the two column-tile MOPAs that use A0, then load A1 and issue the corresponding two MOPAs. This changes instruction scheduling to keep each A vector live only across its two column updates; it does not add ZA state or change reduction order. Keep tail handling and the general path unchanged.
risks: The compiler may already schedule these operations this way, so source changes may produce identical code. A longer live range for A0, or altered scheduling, may increase register pressure or slow the loop. Prior supplied trials were mixed or strongly regressed, and do not establish which changes caused those outcomes. This proposal is unverified.
